nodeData.topic: Day 01 · Verse 2: Everything in the Name, Yet No Taste
nodeData.note: Siksastakam 2 (CC Antya 20.16) · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj shows the two sides of the second verse: the holy name alone gives everything and is available to all, yet we who chant feel no attraction to it. Following Bhaktivinoda Thakura he explains the four causes of this misfortune — weakness of heart, offences, taste for temporary things and illusion about spiritual truth — and says strong, serious sadhana is what frees us. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: In this verse Caitanya Mahaprabhu praises the Lord's many names, full of his energy and easy to chant, and laments that he has no attraction to them. Maharaj says that looked at carefully it has a positive side and a negative side. — “we see the positive and the negative side.”

nodeData.note: Siksastakam 3 (CC Antya 20.21) · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains that the third verse gives the qualification for real chanting: humility and tolerance. He contrasts chanting the 'alphabet' with chanting the holy name, describes today's taking society against the giving society Srila Prabhupada created, and draws lessons from the grass and the tree. In the questions he defines humility as bold and submissive, outlines the five stages of chanting and urges chanting with advanced devotees. nodeData.topic: Day 03 · Verse 4: Not Poverty, but Pure Desire
nodeData.note: Siksastakam 4 (CC Antya 20.29) · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains that the fourth verse is not a vow of poverty or a ban on disciples and family, but a call to stop chasing material things and to let purity, not campaigning, attract people. Desire cannot be killed, only purified, and he closes with the marriage values of his village and with how the whole Siksastakam carries one from cleansing to love of God. nodeData.topic: Day 04 · Verse 5: Somehow Fallen, Begging to Return
nodeData.note: Siksastakam 5 (CC Antya 20.32) · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj calls the fifth verse simple-looking but complex: it covers our material body, our position as souls, and the appeal to be put back in our original service. He explores the 'madness' of accepting a body, what 'somehow or other' and 'fallen' can mean, the soul's in-between position, Indra as a hog, and why real lamentation for our condition is a sign of advancement. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: This verse is Mahaprabhu's plea, as an eternal servant fallen into material life, to be lifted back to Krishna's feet. Maharaj says it looks simple but is very complex. — “It looks very simple but very very complex.”

nodeData.topic: Day 07 · Verse 1: The Ocean of Bliss in the Holy Name
nodeData.note: Siksastakam 1 (CC Antya 20.12) · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing the first verse in Dehradun, Maharaj reviews its seven effects and dwells on the holy name as an ocean of bliss with no end and no danger, unlike the restless ocean of material life. He calls chanting the only investment with a guarantee, says every step is nectar, and in a long Q&A speaks on chanting more rounds, gaining a taste through service, spiritual happiness and why one does not come back from the spiritual world. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 08 · Verse 1: The Name Helps the Helpless
nodeData.note: Siksastakam 1 (CC Antya 20.12) · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Introducing the Siksastakam, Maharaj explains that the holy name first clears away the heart's unwanted things but its real goal is Krishna-prema, and that the name is a conscious person who knows why we call. He teaches chanting in a mood of surrender, begging the devotees for mercy and hearing the sixteen words, and says a devotee who chants properly cannot stay morose. In the questions he speaks on the wandering mind, patience, and how the name answers only the helpless. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 09 · Verse 1: Dust on the Mirror, Fire Put Out
nodeData.note: Siksastakam 1 (CC Antya 20.12) · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj says the eight prayers Caitanya Mahaprabhu himself gave contain everything needed to go from our contaminated state to pure love, and he begins the seven effects of the first verse. He explains the mirror and false pride, the three kinds of dust we heap on ourselves, the fire of material miseries that the name puts out, and the moonlight of good fortune that comes from wholehearted chanting. In the questions he explains surrender as full attention to the name and what changes when we become helpless before Krishna. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.
